texts.preamble: Subhash Chandra vs State Of U.P. And Another on 9 April, 2024 Author: Samit Gopal Bench: Samit Gopal High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad ?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:62295 Court No. - 87 Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 2312 of 2001 Revisionist :- Subhash Chandra Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Revisionist :- Ramanand Pandey Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt.Advocate Hon'ble Samit Gopal,J. 1. List revised.
texts.arguments: At the outset, learned counsel for the revisionist submits that the revisionist has already undergone four months and fourteen days in jail and has also deposited the fine as imposed on him by the trial court. He further submits that he does not challenge his conviction, but submits that he is ready and willing to apply for commutation of sentence on the condition of further deposit, if any, in lieu of awarded sentence. 5. Learned A.G.A. submits that the sentence is proportionate to the charge established. He also submits that no useful purpose would be served by keeping this revision pending and it be disposed of by giving appropriate directions. 6. It is not disputed that the alleged offence took place on 29.10.1995, when the alleged sample of turmeric purchased from the revisionist was found to be adulterated. Learned A.G.A. is right in his submission that this Court cannot tinker, where minimum sentence is provided under a statute like the P.F.A. Act, 1954. 7. The Apex Court in the case of State of Rajasthan Vs. Jagdish Prasad : (2009) 12 SCC 646 held in paras-4 and 5 thereof as under: "4. In Dayal Singh v. State of Rajasthan it was inter alia observed as follows: (SCC pp. 728-29, para 15) "15. In the instant case it was not disputed that for the offence charged a minimum sentence of 6 months' rigorous imprisonment is prescribed by law. The appellant has been sentenced to undergo 6 months' rigorous imprisonment which is the minimum sentence. We are not inclined to modify the sentence by passing an order of the nature passed in N. Sukumaran Nair where this Court in exercise of its extraordinary jurisdiction imposed only a sentence of fine and directed that State to exercise its powers under Section 433 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to commute the sentence of simple imprisonment for fine. Subhash Chandra vs State Of U.P. And Another on 9 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140378102/ 2 If no order in the matter of commutation is passed by the appropriate Government the accused shall surrender to custody to serve the remainder of sentence." Learned counsel for the revisionist has also expressed his willingness that the revisionist is prepared to apply for commutation of sentence under Section 433 of the Code and is also willing to deposit additional fine.
